title: Unmarked cone straightening compared with the ordinary-base comma diagram
statement:
Use simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, internal functor sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and the unmarked ordered-cone straightening of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. Fix a small ordinary category $C$ and any simplicial map $p:X\to N(C)$, in universes large enough for these constructions. Opposite of a simplicial set reverses its ordered vertices: in degree $n$, $d_i^{\mathrm{op}}=d_{n-i}$ and $s_i^{\mathrm{op}}=s_{n-i}$. Regard $C$ and $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ as simplicial categories with discrete mapping sets, put $S=N(C)^{\mathrm{op}}=N(C^{\mathrm{op}})$ and let $\phi:\mathfrak C[S]\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the coherent-realization counit. Let $v$ be the last vertex of the ordered cone on $X^{\mathrm{op}}$, and define the strict $C$-diagram
$$H_C(X)(c)=\bigl(\mathfrak C[X^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X^{\mathrm{op}}]}C^{\mathrm{op}}\bigr)(c,v),$$
with action by precomposition; the attaching map is $\phi\mathfrak C[p^{\mathrm{op}}]$. Define another strict $C$-diagram
$$F_C(X)(c)=X\times_{N(C)}N(C/c),$$
where $C/c$ has objects arrows $d\to c$ and morphisms commuting triangles, and its functor to $C$ takes the source. Thus its degree-$n$ elements are pairs $(x,h:p(x_n)\to c)$; restriction along $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ is $(\theta^*x,h\,p(x_{\theta(m)}\to x_n))$, and the $C$-action postcomposes $h$. Write $F_C(X)^{\mathrm{op}}$ for the diagram taking the simplicial opposite at each value, without changing its indexing category.

There is a natural transformation of strict $C$-diagrams
$$\alpha_{C,X}:H_C(X)\longrightarrow F_C(X)^{\mathrm{op}}$$
whose components are weak homotopy equivalences for every $X$, without any Kan, left-fibration or cofibrancy hypothesis on $X$. Specify the transformation by the following simplex normalization and colimit extension. For $C=[r]$ and $X=N([r])$ with its identity base map, put $\mathcal P_i=\{J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,i\}:i\in J\}$, ordered by inclusion. The cube $N(\mathcal P_i)=\mathfrak C[X^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^0](i,v)$ maps surjectively onto $H_{[r]}(X)(i)$ through the cone pushout: its relations identify the images of every mapping simplex in $\mathfrak C[X^{\mathrm{op}}](a,b)$ with the unique arrow $a\to b$ in $[r]^{\mathrm{op}}$, also after composing with a cone mapping simplex. Thus this is a quotient of the cube, not an identification with the cube itself. Define $\alpha_{[r],X}(i)$ as the map induced on this quotient by
$$N(\mathcal P_i)\longrightarrow N(\{0,\ldots,i\}^{\mathrm{op}})=F_{[r]}(X)(i)^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad J\longmapsto\min J.$$
The displayed nerve map descends through these pushout relations, and its descended map is $\alpha_{[r],X}(i)$. The $[r]$-action from $i$ to $j$ is induced by adding $j$ to a subset. For a simplex $\sigma:[r]\to C$, extend this normalized map by left Kan extension along $\sigma$, and then extend over the category of simplices of $X$ by colimits. Here left Kan extension $u_!$ of strict simplicial-set diagrams is characterized by $\operatorname{Nat}(u_!A,B)=\operatorname{Nat}(A,Bu)$; both $H$ and $F$ have the canonical identifications $u_!H_C(X)=H_D(N(u)_!X)$ and $u_!F_C(X)=F_D(N(u)_!X)$, where $N(u)_!$ composes the base map with $N(u)$. This specification is well defined and natural in $X$ and in functors $u:C\to D$, with these identifications, and respects their identities and composites.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.10 (the natural map, simplex normalization, and colimit/left-Kan-extension specification), Lemma 3.2.5.17(1) (objectwise weak homotopy equivalence for every simplicial input); Remark 3.2.5.5 and Example 3.2.5.6 identify F with the displayed comma pullback. Read in the retained sandbox PDF, printed pages 195–198 and 201–202. No Stacks tag states this unmarked comparison. Local literature archive WANTED. The simplex map is specified through the actual cone-pushout quotient; no identification of that quotient with the unquotiented subset cube is asserted.

from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, the finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction before taking the derived inverse limit; foundational notions for the operadic enrichment used by lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus. Defines the complete operadic enriched categories and their coefficients used by that mapping-complex construction. The Kan-valued relative-nerve construction justifies the object-space indexing left fibration used to define algebroids. Ordinary-base adjoint comparison identifies the classifying functor of the explicit relative-nerve indexing construction after its left-fibration property has been proved. Technical comparison of the ordinary-base cone straightening with the explicit quotient left adjoint, for every simplicial input, before any fibrancy assumption.
